title: 3675. Minimum Operations to Transform String

examples.explanation: Change 'y' to 'z' to get "zz". Change 'z' to 'a' to get "aa". Thus, the answer is 2.
The string "a" only consists of 'a' characters. Thus, the answer is 0.

hints: Each operation shifts every occurrence of a chosen character forward by one in the alphabet (with wrap-around).
For any character c, the number of moves required to turn it into 'a' is (26 - (ord(c) - ord('a'))) % 26.

You can plan operations so characters that need more shifts are advanced first and cause merges that don't increase the total number of moves; therefore the minimum number of moves equals the maximum, over characters appearing in s, of (26 - (ord(c) - ord('a'))) % 26.
